people.match_note: one of the Eaton brothers, probably Howard

people.name: Edward S. Allen
people.bio: Edward S. Allen was listed as the plaintiff's attorney in a Morton County sheriff's sale notice that ran from May to June 1886. In September 1886 a letter to the Cow Boy signed by F. B. & E. S. Allen, attorneys for the N. P. Refrigerator Car Co., corrected the paper's report on the company's tax suits.

moments.label: Named plaintiff's attorney in a sheriff's sale

people.name: Edwin Bulpin
people.role: Medora telegraph operator and railroad agent
people.bio: Edwin Bulpin was Medora's telegraph operator and in February 1884 was also made express, freight and ticket agent, and the paper ran a comic poem about his hunting. In March 1884 he resigned to take a telegraph job on the Utah Northern in Idaho, and Hugh Flynn replaced him.

moments.label: Appointed express, freight and ticket agent
Left for a telegraph job in Idaho

people.name: F. H. Eaton
people.role: Pittsburgh man who summered at the Logging Camp, 1886
people.bio: F. H. Eaton of Pittsburgh arrived in March 1886 with Miss Hattie Eaton to spend the summer at the Logging Camp, and in June the paper quoted his delight at coming in from the Logging Camp soaked through by rain. In October 1886 he was called back to Pittsburgh by the serious illness of his son-in-law.

moments.label: Arrived from Pittsburgh to summer at the Logging Camp
Called home by his son-in-law's illness

people.name: George Auld
people.role: Belfield newspaper editor and hay seller
people.bio: George Auld of Belfield was co-editor with Louis C. Hay of a newspaper published by the Mandan Times in 1885, and he visited Medora on business. In March 1886 he came to sell the hay he and Frank Holmes had put up, about seventy tons left of three hundred.

moments.label: Named co-editor with Louis C. Hay
Sold leftover hay in Medora

people.name: George Smith
people.role: Medora horseman in charge at Sully creek ranch, 1884
people.bio: George Smith gave curiosities to the Cow Boy's museum in February 1884 and was badly bitten by the Kentucky stallion that May, when he was also put in charge of the stock horses at Sully creek ranch. In July 1884 he narrowly escaped injury when a team of broncos he was holding ran away toward the Cow Boy office.

moments.label: Put in charge of stock horses at Sully creek
Escaped injury in a bronco runaway

people.name: George W. Towers
people.bio: George W. Towers was a stockman who took part in the round-up meeting of April 1884 and at the association's meeting in April 1885 was named to a committee to see that a stock inspector was appointed for Medora. In March 1886 he was named to a committee at the Mingusville stockmen's meeting.

moments.label: Named to stock-inspector committee
Named to committee at the Mingusville meeting

people.name: Harry Gregg
people.bio: Harry Gregg of Spearfish, a former superintendent of the Homestake mine, was a Lawrence County legislator who passed through Medora in January 1885 and promised to work for repeal of the herd law. When the fence law passed in March 1885, the paper credited him and the other Black Hills members.

moments.label: Pledged support for herd-law repeal
Credited with passing the fence law

people.name: Henry W. Coe
people.bio: Dr. Henry W. Coe of Mandan was nominated for the territorial legislature in October 1884 and represented Medora's district. In 1885 he closed up Coll McClellan's census work at Medora, and in fall 1886 he inspected an Oliver County herd reported to have pleuro-pneumonia.

moments.label: Nominated for the territorial legislature
Inspected a herd reported to have pleuro-pneumonia

people.name: J. J. Hill
people.role: St. Paul railroad man (Manitoba Road) and Aberdeen-Angus breeder
people.bio: The St. Paul railroad builder appears as a breeder of Aberdeen-Angus cattle, buying a small herd in Scotland in 1885 and taking first prize at the Chicago Fat Stock Show that November; in January 1886 the paper reported further Chicago honors for his steers, including Benholm. In December 1886 the paper reported him pressing for a bill giving his Manitoba Road right of way across the Fort Berthold and Blackfeet reservations.

moments.label: Won first prize at the Chicago Fat Stock Show
Sought railroad right of way across two reservations

people.name: J. P. Small
people.role: Glendive cattleman handling the LC herd
people.bio: J. P. Small of Glendive came to Medora at the end of August 1885 to arrange the transfer of the LC cattle, though in September it was decided to leave the herd in the Bad Lands. He attended the April 1886 stock meeting with his son and at the end of August 1886 sold sixty head of LC cattle in Chicago.

moments.label: Arranged transfer of the LC cattle
Marketed sixty LC cattle in Chicago

people.name: J. W. Gallup
people.bio: J. W. Gallup was a Cave Hills ranchman who in March 1885 came to Medora to get his papers as postmaster at Cave Hills, and in April reported cattle losses in the Cave Hills a little above average, heaviest for the Hashknife outfit. By February 1886 Aleck Connell had bought out his Cave Hills ranch.

moments.label: Came to Medora to be made Cave Hills postmaster
His Cave Hills ranch reported bought by Aleck Connell

people.name: Jack Bullion
people.role: Horseman with a ranch on Bullion creek
people.bio: Jack Bullion brought about thirty horses in for the round-up in June 1884 and in 1885 had a ranch on Bullion creek, where his brother Robert from Minnesota joined him with horses. At the end of November 1885 sixteen of his ponies were sold at about twenty dollars each.

moments.label: Brought in about thirty horses for the round-up
Sold sixteen ponies at about $20 each

people.name: Jack Tisdale
people.role: Northern Pacific employee; later at the Elkhorn ranch
people.bio: Jack Tisdale worked for the Northern Pacific and married in May 1886, when he and his wife were welcomed at Medora. By December 1886 they were keeping house at the Elkhorn ranch, and warrants were issued for his arrest as an accessory in the case against George Myers.

moments.label: Keeping house with his wife at the Elkhorn ranch
Warrant issued as accessory in the George Myers case

people.name: James Wishart
people.role: Freighter on the Black Hills routes
people.bio: James 'Jim' Wishart was an old-time freighter whose outfit hauled freight through Medora in 1884 and brought Rassie Deffebach's family and goods to town that August. In November 1885 the paper reported the death in Deadwood of his wife, who drove a string team alongside him.

moments.label: Wife, also a teamster, died in Deadwood

people.name: John B. Raymond
people.bio: John B. Raymond, Dakota's delegate to Congress, passed through Medora in July 1884 and faced a stiff fight for renomination at the Pierre convention that September. The paper reported his wife's burial in February 1885 and, in January 1886, the death of "Hon. John B. Raymond of Fargo."

moments.label: Faced opposition at the Pierre nominating convention
Death reported

people.name: John McGee
people.role: Contractor who built the Medora slaughter-house
people.bio: John McGee was foreman of a carpenter crew in December 1884 and the contractor who finished the slaughter-house in 1885, a building the paper called equal to any of its kind in the United States. In January 1885 he was thinking of settling in Medora to build, and in September he left for Jamestown after the finishing touches.

moments.label: Finished work on the slaughter-house
Left for Jamestown after completing the slaughter-house

people.name: John P. Belding
people.bio: John P. Belding, ex-sheriff of Lawrence County and a capital commissioner, traveled through Medora between Deadwood and the East in 1884, once arriving only thirty-six hours from Deadwood. In early 1885 he was in Bismarck, where he was elected president, or speaker, of the "third house."

moments.label: Passed through, thirty-six hours from Deadwood
Elected president of the 'third house' at Bismarck

people.name: John S. Seaton
people.bio: John S. ("Uncle John") Seaton was an old Medora hand who in March 1885 sent the paper, from Yonkers, New York, an account of the adventures of the Jones & Pennell outfit. He returned from the Black Hills in March 1886 to keep books for Bob Roberts, and in June 1886 the paper ran a comic account of a vagrancy trial in "Judge Seaton's court."

moments.label: Returned from the Black Hills to stay the summer
Named as judge in a comic account of a vagrancy trial

people.match_note: Judge Seaton merged as the only Seaton in Medora

people.name: John Sechler
people.bio: John Sechler, known as "Arkansas John," was a freighter of 26 years whose mule train could haul 100,000 pounds and who arrived at Medora in late May 1884. The paper cited him in July 1884 as one of the freighters who called the Medora route to the Black Hills the best.

moments.label: Arrived in Medora with his large mule train

people.name: Johnny Chute
people.role: Medora bartender and roller rink racer
people.bio: Johnny Chute was serving drinks at a Medora saloon in February 1885, and that spring he shot with the gun club and won races at the roller rink. In December 1886 the paper listed him among old-timers as last heard of in Helena.

moments.label: Won the potato race at the rink

people.name: Lieut. Varnum
people.role: 7th Cavalry lieutenant surveying Black Hills routes
people.bio: Lieut. Varnum of the 7th Cavalry surveyed official routes to Fort Meade in summer 1884, finishing the Dickinson route, working on the Belfield route, and passing through with a squad of men on the Medora road; the Cow Boy's party overtook his outfit on its own trip to the Hills. In December 1886 the paper reported that Miss Mollie Moore had recently married Lt. Varnum.

moments.label: Completed the Dickinson-Fort Meade route survey
Reported married to Miss Mollie Moore

people.name: M. G. Hall
people.role: Assistant superintendent of the Northern Pacific Express Co.
people.bio: M. G. Hall was assistant superintendent of the Northern Pacific Express Co. and passed through Medora on the railroad in 1884. In November 1885 he resigned after a long time in that post to take the company's agency at St. Paul.

moments.label: Arrived as N. P. Express assistant superintendent

people.match_note: M. J. Hall (invited on first Deadwood stage, Oct 1884) taken as a misprint of M. G. Hall

people.name: Mike Finnegan
people.role: Medora "bad man" convicted of stealing Roosevelt's Elkhorn boat
people.bio: Mike Finnegan, whom the Cow Boy mocked as "Mr. Bad Man Finnegan," was disarmed by Fred Willard in December 1885 after a drunken display with a rifle, and in April 1886 was accused of stealing a row-boat from the Elkhorn ranch of Theodore Roosevelt, the future president, then a Bad Lands rancher. Brought back, sent to Mandan for trial, he and a partner pleaded guilty to grand larceny in August 1886 and were each sentenced to twenty-five months; in November the paper reported him in the Bismarck penitentiary.

moments.label: Accused of stealing the Elkhorn ranch boat
Pleaded guilty, sentenced to twenty-five months

people.name: Mrs. J. A. McGregor
people.bio: Mrs. J. A. McGregor helped host the editor's party at Wadsworth's ranch in June 1884, and in February 1885 and October 1886 came in to visit Mrs. Paddock. In October 1886 she left for her home in Berlin Heights, Ohio.

moments.label: Helped host visitors at Wadsworth's ranch
Left for her home in Berlin Heights, Ohio

people.name: N. A. Thayer
people.role: Northern Pacific assistant superintendent of bridges and buildings
people.bio: N. A. Thayer was the Northern Pacific's assistant superintendent of bridges and buildings for the division and oversaw railroad work at Medora in 1884 and 1885. In January 1886 he and his bridge crew repaired the bridge after cold weather pulled it out of shape.

moments.label: Identified as assistant superintendent of bridges and buildings
Repaired the bridge damaged by cold weather

people.name: P. D. Cravath
people.role: Minneapolis visitor and the editor's companion to the Black Hills
people.bio: P. D. Cravath of Minneapolis, an old college friend of the Cow Boy's editor, set out with him for the Black Hills at the end of June 1884. The paper calls him both a representative of the Globe Oil Works and a correspondent of the Minneapolis Tribune.

moments.label: Joined the editor's camping trip to the Black Hills

people.name: P. S. Bemis
people.role: New Yorker who cowboyed on the Little Missouri
people.bio: P. S. "Tap" Bemis of New York, lately of Ransom County, joined the round-up at Medora in September 1885 to learn the cattle business. After more than a year cowpunching on the river, he left in September 1886 to run a wagon for an Arizona outfit owned by New York friends.

moments.label: Joined the round-up to learn the cattle business
Left to run a wagon for an Arizona outfit

people.match_note: 'Tap' Bemis taken as P. S. Bemis

people.name: Paddock
people.role: Medora old-timer; stock association committeeman and gun club member
people.bio: Paddock was a Medora old-timer who in March 1884 sat on the committee of five drafting by-laws for the Bad Lands Live Stock Association, and whose boar was matched against Pennell & Roberts' bears for a $50-a-side fight that April. He shot with the Bad Lands Gun Club in 1885 and came back from a late-November 1885 hunt with Fisher and McGregor bringing thirteen deer and eighty-five prairie chickens.

moments.label: Sat on committee drafting stock association by-laws
Returned from hunt with thirteen deer

people.match_note: Mostly E. G. Paddock, but Billy Paddock was also active.

people.name: Paul Heinze
people.bio: Paul Heinze, a Bismarck surveyor, finished resurveying the Medora town-plat in May 1885, finding the earlier survey off by six inches to four feet. In September 1885 he surveyed the scene of the shooting in which Luffsey was killed and showed his sketch at the trial, while cowboys passing by mistook his transit for a camera and posed for him.

moments.label: Completed survey of the Medora town-plat
Presented sketch of the Luffsey shooting scene

people.match_note: Bare 'Heinze' (Medora town-plat survey) assumed same

people.name: R. H. Moore
people.bio: R. H. Moore was listed as foreman in the round-up district notices printed in spring 1885. He was again named foreman in a September 1885 item.

moments.label: Listed as foreman in round-up district notice

people.name: Scott
people.bio: Under the name Scott the paper refers to Editor Scott of the Dickinson Press, its rival in a 1884 argument over the Medora freight route, who married that spring. A different Scott appears in August 1886 as the partner of a prisoner, who escaped from Dickinson and had not been heard from.

moments.label: Sparred with the Cow Boy over the Medora freight route

people.match_note: mixed contexts; one is an 'Editor Scott' near Dickinson

people.name: W. B. Wright
people.role: Medora resident from the East; association secretary
people.bio: W. B. Wright arrived from New York with a Mr. Baird in April 1884, gave $50 for the injured Frank Walker in March 1885 and served as secretary of a church society formed that June. By December 1886 the paper listed him among old-timers, then living in Cromwell, Mass.

moments.label: Served as secretary of a new association
Listed as an old-timer now in Cromwell, Mass.

people.name: W. W. Mabee
people.bio: W. W. Mabee of the Glendive Times attended the April 1885 stock meeting and was elected secretary of the North of Yellowstone meeting. The Cow Boy disputed one of his statements in September 1885, and he attended the April 1886 Little Missouri River Stockgrowers' meeting.

moments.label: Elected secretary of the North of Yellowstone meeting
Attended the Little Missouri stockgrowers' meeting

people.name: William M. Brewer
people.role: Former Minnesela Boomer editor; helped issue the Cow Boy
people.bio: William M. "Billy" Brewer, late editor of the Minnesela Boomer, came to Medora from Deadwood in June 1884 and helped issue the Cow Boy while the editor was away that July. He also branded calves at Wadsworth's ranch before leaving for home in Deadwood later that month.

moments.label: Helped issue the Cow Boy during the editor's absence

people.match_note: Billy Brewer and the bare Brewer (helped issue the paper in Packard's absence) taken as W. M. Brewer

people.name: William Miller
people.role: Minnesela, Dakota, man seeking strayed horses
people.bio: William Miller of Minnesela, Butte County, advertised in the Cow Boy in December 1884 for horses that had strayed on Grand river. In January 1885 the paper cited his case in an editorial comment.

moments.label: Advertised strayed horses
Paper commented on his lost-horse case

people.name: Wm. R. Snider
people.role: Major, editor of the Spearfish Register
people.bio: Maj. W. R. Snider, editor of the Spearfish Register, visited Medora in April 1884. In May 1884 the Cow Boy reprinted a Black Hills Pioneer item calling him the best editorial writer in Dakota and reporting his belief that a railroad from the Northern Pacific would soon be built. In July 1884 he and Dr. Louthan showed the Cow Boy's party around Spearfish.

moments.label: Called the best editorial writer in Dakota
Guided the Cow Boy party around Spearfish

people.name: A. J. Morton
people.bio: Dr. A. J. Morton of Iowa, whose father farmed at South Heart, announced his practice in June 1884, giving Medora its first local physician. In July 1884 he brought wheat, oats and barley from his father's farm for display at the Cow Boy office.

moments.label: Announced practice as Medora's first local physician

people.name: A. N. Jeffries
people.role: Cattleman with a ranch down the Little Missouri
people.bio: A. N. Jeffries returned from Albany, Texas, in March 1886 to his ranch down the river, reporting that his company would drive about 10,000 head of cattle that year, and in April planned an outfit to work the river below the round-up district. In August 1886 he was elected vice-chairman of the Little Missouri River Stockgrowers' Association.

moments.label: Reported his company would drive about 10,000 cattle
Elected vice-chairman of the stockgrowers' association

people.name: Adolph Eyraud
people.bio: Adolph Eyraud was the Marquis de Mores' gardener, working on hot-beds and transplanting in the bottom south of the Marquis' house in spring 1884. By June 1884 a force-pump was watering the garden.

moments.label: Improving the Marquis' garden with hot-beds

people.name: Billy Paddock
people.role: Bad Lands rancher who sold his ranch to Lamb & Holland
people.bio: In March 1885 Billy Paddock sold his ranch down the Little Missouri to Lamb & Holland of Boston, who planned to stock it with cattle. In November 1885 he went down the river on a hunting trip.

moments.label: Sold his ranch to Lamb & Holland of Boston

people.match_note: Distinct from E. G. Paddock ('Messrs. E. G. and Billy Paddock'). Possibly the Wm. Paddock later in Wadena, Minn., but kept apart.

people.name: Bond
people.role: Ranch partner of Tarbell at the Custer Trail and Deep Creek ranches
people.bio: Bond was Tarbell's partner, living at the Custer Trail ranch in July 1884 and at their Deep Creek ranch by March 1885. In September 1885 the two received a lot of horses in town.

moments.label: Living with Tarbell at the Custer Trail ranch

people.match_note: Could be G. G. or A. H. Bond

people.name: Calamity Joe
people.bio: "Calamity Joe" escaped a deputy at gunpoint at Rapid City and was captured in February 1886 at Glenullin by Stark County Sheriff Sebastian and Deputy Goudy. Held wounded in the Dickinson jail, he waived examination on a horse-stealing charge in March 1886 and was bound over in $1,000.

moments.label: Captured at Glenullin by Stark County officers
Bound over on a horse-stealing charge

people.name: Charles M. Tibbetts
people.role: Slaughter-house pipefitter, then night engineer and watchman
people.bio: Charles M. Tibbetts did piping and fitting work at the slaughter-house with Houlihan, praised in July 1885. In August 1885 he became night engineer and watchman there.

moments.label: Praised for pipefitting at the slaughter-house
Became night engineer and watchman

people.name: Chas. Shaffer
people.role: Former partner in Shaffer & Munroe, Plum Grove ranch
people.bio: Chas. Shaffer was a partner with John Munroe in Shaffer & Munroe, of the Plum Grove ranch on the Little Missouri. The partnership was dissolved by mutual consent on May 24, 1884, a notice the Cow Boy ran through June.

moments.label: Dissolved partnership in Shaffer & Munroe, Plum Grove ranch

people.name: Clay Layton
people.role: Horse thief, partner of Henry Scott
people.bio: Clay Layton and Henry Scott were arrested near Miles City in August 1884 for stealing four horses from Archie Morton of South Heart, and escaped from the Dickinson jail that September. He was rearrested at Buffalo Gap in 1886 and sentenced at Mandan to five years and eight months in the Bismarck penitentiary.

moments.label: Escaped from the Dickinson jail with Henry Scott
Sentenced to five years eight months in prison

people.name: Col. McClellan
people.role: First census enumerator for Billings County
people.bio: Col. McClellan was named the first census enumerator for Billings County in June 1885. He left in August 1885 to farm near Moorhead.

moments.label: Named first census enumerator for Billings County

people.name: D. M. McIntosh
people.bio: Dr. D. M. McIntosh of Glendive made professional visits to Medora in 1884, including treating Mrs. Fitzgerald's sick baby. In May 1885 the paper reported that he and Dr. Robarts had operated to remove a tumor from Mrs. Draper.

moments.label: Treated Mrs. Fitzgerald's sick baby

people.name: Ed. Turner
people.bio: Ed. Turner went to the O'Fallon creek round-up in May 1886 with Al. Uhlrich and George Myers. In November 1886 he married Kate Goodall and left on a wedding trip west to Oregon.

moments.label: Married Miss Kate Goodall

people.name: G. G. Cooper
people.bio: G. G. Cooper was day telegraph operator at Medora until April 1885, when he moved to a corresponding position at Billings, where the paper said he earned a reputation as one of the best operators on the road. By September 1886 he was working for Western Union in St. Paul.

moments.label: Left Medora for an operator's post at Billings
Working for Western Union in St. Paul

people.name: George Cole
people.role: Representative of the N. P. Refrigerator Car Co.
people.bio: George Cole appears in the Cow Boy in 1885 and 1886. In April 1886, as the company's representative, he had the papers served in the injunction stopping Stark County's treasurer from collecting taxes in Billings County.

moments.label: Served injunction papers on Stark County's treasurer

people.name: George Fraser
people.role: Refrigerator Car Co. cowboy killed by lightning, 1886
people.bio: George Fraser rode for the Refrigerator Car Co. and went to the Hashknife camp with Riley Brooks in May 1886. He was killed by lightning in late August 1886, and the Cow Boy condemned the Bismarck Tribune for falsely reporting that the sheriff had killed two cowboys.

moments.label: Killed by a lightning strike

people.name: George Heywood
people.role: Wounded by Bob Roberts in a Medora saloon
people.bio: George Heywood was shot in November 1884 by Bob Roberts in Roberts' Medora saloon. Reports said Heywood had come in armed and threatened to kill Roberts, and the wound in his left breast was not fatal and healed well.

moments.label: Wounded in a shooting with Bob Roberts
Reported to have entered the saloon armed

people.name: George T. Reynolds
people.role: Albany, Texas, cattleman; brother of B. F. Reynolds
people.bio: George T. Reynolds of Albany, Texas, announced in January 1885 that he would put about eight thousand Texas steers on the range a few miles down the Little Missouri that summer. In late August 1885 his brother B. F. Reynolds took charge of the cattle, which arrived at Mingusville in fine condition, while he went east.

moments.label: Planned to range eight thousand Texas steers downriver
Cattle arrived at Mingusville; brother took charge

people.match_note: 'Geo. W.' / 'G. W.' (brother of B. F., Albany, Texas) taken as misprints of Geo. T.; unsure.

people.name: Gideon C. Moody
people.role: Judge of Deadwood; senator-elect of the proposed state of Dakota
people.bio: Judge G. C. Moody of Deadwood was elected one of two senators in December 1885 by the legislature of the proposed state of southern Dakota meeting at Huron, which the Cow Boy called a farce. In January 1886 he was given the privilege of the floor of the U.S. Senate, recognition the paper doubted would go further.

moments.label: Elected senator by the Huron legislature
Admitted to the floor of the Senate

people.name: H. F. Fountain
people.bio: H. F. Fountain kept a store at Mingusville in 1886. The paper praised his stock of goods in April 1886.

moments.label: Praised for his store's assortment at Mingusville

people.name: H. R. Mead
people.bio: Miss H. R. Mead, of the Bismarck firm H. R. Mead & Co., sold millinery and dry goods. She came from Dickinson and opened for business at the Pyramid Park hotel in October 1884, and Miss Mead was in Medora with millinery goods in May 1885.

moments.label: Opened millinery sales at the Pyramid Park hotel
Brought millinery goods to Medora

people.name: Harriman
people.bio: Harriman passed through in May 1884 claiming to be walking from Duluth to San Francisco and to be a champion six-day pedestrian. The paper soon called him exposed as a tramp who rode freight trains.

moments.label: Exposed by the paper as a tramp, not a walker

people.name: Harvey T. Halleck
people.role: Cattle investor from Washington, Pa., later of Mandan
people.bio: Harvey T. Halleck of Washington, Pennsylvania, spent several days in Medora in June 1884 arranging to put cattle on Tepee bottom. By 1886 he lived at Mandan in Morton County, and in May and June that year the paper printed a notice listing him as a partner in the LeMoyne Cattle Co., Limited.

moments.label: Arranged to put cattle on Tepee bottom

people.name: Henry L. Dawes
people.role: U.S. senator from Massachusetts on Indian affairs
people.bio: Henry L. Dawes, a Massachusetts senator the paper called a friend of the Indians, was in 1885 on the congressional committee before which a lease of the Crow reservation, which the Cow Boy called a swindle, would come. In 1885 he and Senator Ingalls, as a Senate subcommittee, were to visit the Indian Territory, and his party was expected to come as far north as the southern limit of the Crow reservation. In December the paper mocked his 'ultra-philanthropic constituents' in an editorial on the Apaches.

moments.label: On committee to hear the Crow reservation lease
Named to inspect the Indian Territory

people.name: J. A. Freeze
people.bio: J. A. Freeze lived in Medora in 1885, when a female member of his family died of cholera infantum in August and was buried on the coal mine butte. He solicited orders for enlarging photographs, working Glendive in October 1885, and moved his family to Glendive in February 1886.

moments.label: Solicited photograph-enlarging orders in Glendive
Moved with his family to Glendive

people.name: J. J. Clemmer
people.role: Cresco, Iowa, partner in the Clemmer & Dell Cave Hills ranch
people.bio: J. J. Clemmer of Cresco, Iowa, was a partner in the Clemmer & Dell cattle ranch in the Cave Hills and in 1885 planned to use Polled-Angus bulls only. In August 1885 he reported an Aberdeen-Angus calf that gained 150 pounds in forty days on grass.

moments.label: Switched his Cave Hills herd to Polled-Angus bulls

people.name: J. Juelfs
people.bio: J. Juelfs brought his bull-team outfit up from Deadwood in May 1884 to haul freight over the Medora route. In June 1884 it pulled out with 75,000 pounds of freight.

moments.label: Bull outfit left with 75,000 pounds of freight

people.name: J. M. Hannaford
people.role: General freight agent of the Northern Pacific
people.bio: J. M. Hannaford was the Northern Pacific's general freight agent. In July 1884 his word that freight cars need not be unloaded until fall figured in the Cow Boy's quarrel over a Medora freight house, and in July 1885 he reported 98,000 cattle shipped west over the road the year before.

moments.label: Reported 98,000 cattle shipped west in 1884

people.name: J. W. Harbison
people.bio: J. W. Harbison was postmaster at Belfield, who left for his former home in New York in April 1884 with the paper hinting he would return married. In October 1884 he was elected a delegate at the Billings county convention held at Belfield.

moments.label: Left for New York, expected to marry
Elected delegate at Billings county convention

people.name: James Riley
people.role: Medora resident who raised money for the school
people.bio: James Riley and Mr. Coleman circulated a petition in November 1884 that raised enough money to open a Medora school at the Cantonment, and in March 1886 he and Mr. Garver ran a contribution box to keep the school going. In October 1886 the paper reported him back in charge at the tank-house.

moments.label: Raised subscriptions to open a Medora school

people.match_note: School-fund mentions in 1884 and 1886 merged; unsure.

people.name: Joe Meyer
people.bio: In September 1885 Joe Meyer's mother wrote from Aurora, Ill., asking his whereabouts, and in February 1886 "Calamity Joe" was arrested in Deadwood for stealing horses near Dickinson. In August 1886 the grand jury at Mandan found the evidence too weak to indict, but Judge Francis held him on $1,000 bond for the next grand jury.

moments.label: Arrested in Deadwood for horse stealing
Grand jury declined to indict; held on bond

people.name: John A. Logan
people.role: U.S. Senator from Illinois; 1884 Republican vice-presidential nominee
people.bio: John A. Logan, the Illinois senator and Union general, was James G. Blaine's running mate in 1884, and the Cow Boy predicted their election. It reported his re-election to the Senate in May 1885.

moments.label: Paper predicted Blaine and Logan would win
Re-elected to the U.S. Senate by Illinois

people.name: John Gallop
people.role: Black Hills freighter (Guild and Gallop; Gallop & Walton)
people.bio: John Gallop kept a stopping place on the road to the Black Hills, where a party traveling the new freight route was put up in April 1884, and with Guild, as Guild and Gallop, hoped to build a railroad from De Mores to the Hay Creek coal mines. In December 1884 the outfit of Gallop & Walton loaded Hills freight at Medora.

moments.label: Hosted freight-route travelers overnight
Planned a railroad to the Hay Creek coal mines

people.name: John Guild
people.role: Backer of the Hay Creek coal road and De Mores townsite
people.bio: John Guild, described in May 1884 as of New York, was one of the company that laid out the townsite of De Mores at the junction of the Redwater and Belle Fourche. In June 1884 he and Gallop traveled from Medora to the Hills by chartered team, and in July the paper reported them planning a railroad from De Mores to the Hay Creek coal mines. In November 1885 the paper reported him at Spearfish as the backer of the Hay Creek coal road.

moments.label: Planned railroad from De Mores to Hay Creek coal mines
Reported at Spearfish backing the Hay Creek coal road

people.name: John Nelson
people.bio: John Nelson planned a dairy with Frank Moore in February 1884, but that month the paper reported it was unclear whether he had failed in business, as his goods had disappeared. By late March 1884 J. A. Ferris had opened a dry goods store in the building Nelson had occupied.

moments.label: Business reported in doubt as his goods disappeared
Ferris opened a store in his former building

people.name: Joseph Nimmo, Jr.
people.role: Chief of the federal Bureau of Statistics; range-cattle writer
people.bio: Joseph Nimmo, Jr., chief of the Bureau of Statistics, wrote the government report on the range and ranch cattle business that the Cow Boy drew on for figures in July 1885. In November 1886 the paper reprinted his Harper's article on the American cowboy.

moments.label: His range-cattle report supplied the paper's figures
Harper's article on the cowboy reprinted

people.name: Josie Maxwell
people.role: Wife of agent J. N. Maxwell, née Smith
people.bio: Josie Maxwell, née Smith, married railroad and express agent J. N. Maxwell in September 1885, and at the end of 1885 the couple were preparing to leave Medora for St. Paul, where he had taken a Wells-Fargo messenger's run. In December 1886 she was visiting her husband's parents in Port Byron, Ill.

moments.label: Married J. N. Maxwell
Visiting her husband's parents in Port Byron, Ill.

people.name: Judge Gordon
people.bio: Gordon, called "Judge," presided over a burlesque court at Medora in July 1885, hearing a mock assault case against Robert Roberts brought by a train-riding drifter. Visitors from Warren, Pennsylvania, sent him a box of cigars that October, and that month the paper named him as a likely justice of the peace if the county organized.

moments.label: Presided over the mock trial of Territory vs. R. Roberts

people.match_note: possibly T. W. Gordon; kept apart

people.name: Julia Butler
people.bio: Julia Butler married James Butler at the Catholic church in Medora, with Father Martin officiating, and the couple set up housekeeping at the Cantonment in January 1885. In July 1886 she left to join her husband, then working on the railroad in the Black Hills.

moments.label: Married James Butler at Medora's Catholic church
Left to join her husband in the Black Hills

people.name: L. D. Pettit
people.role: Bone buyer and stage owner based at Belfield
people.bio: L. D. Pettit of Deadwood made Belfield his headquarters in 1884, holding heavy contracts for bones and paying pickers $8 a ton in cash. His family arrived from Crook City in one of his stages in August 1884, and that September he was building a residence there.

moments.label: Paying $8 a ton for bones at Belfield
Built a residence at Belfield

people.name: L. Q. C. Lamar
people.bio: The Secretary of the Interior in President Cleveland's cabinet was criticized by the Cow Boy in July 1885 for ordering the Texas cattle trails opened against the wishes of the states, territories and stock associations along them. In September 1886 the paper reported his final ruling that the contested Hawkes claim in Deadwood was mineral land, costing business owners their improvements.

moments.label: Ordered the Texas cattle trails opened
Ruled the Deadwood Hawkes claim mineral land

people.name: Lauren Dunlap
people.role: Dakota Commissioner of Immigration, at Huron
people.bio: Lauren Dunlap was Dakota's Commissioner of Immigration, based at Huron, and the Cow Boy summarized his monthly bulletins on weather, crops and conditions in the territory in 1885 and 1886. His August 1886 bulletin complained that the territory's assessed valuation would have been higher had assessors followed the territorial secretary's directions.

moments.label: Paper summarized his September bulletin
His bulletin criticized territorial assessors

people.name: Lillie Roberts
people.role: Young woman of the Medora area
people.bio: Miss Lillie Roberts spent fall 1885 as a guest in the area and visited Medora in February 1886. In December 1886 the paper reported her marriage to Riley Brooks, then retracted it as untrue and apologized to her.

moments.label: Paper apologized for a false marriage report

people.name: Lord Salisbury
people.role: British Conservative leader and prime minister
people.bio: The British Conservative leader appeared in the Cow Boy's foreign news in 1885 as the new prime minister facing chaotic foreign and Irish policy, and he was reported to want an alliance with Germany against Russia. In February 1886 the paper reported that Gladstone had defeated him and was forming a new cabinet.

moments.label: Reported taking office as prime minister
Reported defeated by Gladstone

people.name: M. C. Conners
people.bio: M. C. Conners of Spearfish came to sell beef cattle to the company in 1884 and shipped a trainload to Chicago in 1885. In August 1886 he shipped forty-eight cars of cattle from Mingusville, and in September he passed through Medora following the first of five trains of his cattle shipped from there.

moments.label: Shipped 48 cars of cattle from Mingusville

people.name: M. Kline
people.role: Mandan cigar maker, maker of the "De Mores" brand
people.bio: M. Kline of Mandan advertised in the Cow Boy in early 1884 and made a cigar brand called the "De Mores," which the paper said was already a favorite. In March 1884 he wrote that he would come to Medora to see the dealers, and in June 1884 he spent three days in town, when the boys put him on a bronco that ran away with him four times.

moments.label: Introduced the 'De Mores' cigar brand

people.name: Margaret Gardient
people.role: Young Medora woman, married at Bismarck in May 1885
people.bio: Miss Maggie Gardient was named in March 1885 among the entertainers for a Stockmen's ball at the Pyramid Park hotel, and in April she won first prize among the ladies at a masquerade skating contest. She was married at Bismarck in May 1885; the paper named her as the daughter of Joseph Gardient of New Richland, Minn.

moments.label: Won first prize at a roller rink contest
Married at Bismarck

people.name: Mark Bateman
people.role: Justice of the peace at Mandan
people.bio: Mark Bateman was a justice at Mandan who heard evidence in a death inquiry in April 1884 and, with Justice Collins, discharged the Marquis de Mores in the Luffsey killing on the ground of self-defense. At the Marquis's September 1885 trial at Bismarck he testified about that earlier examination.

moments.label: Earlier acquittal of de Mores in Luffsey case recalled
Testified at de Mores trial about his examination

people.name: Mary Brophy
people.bio: Mary Brophy of Mingusville visited Medora with Annie Brophy in November 1884 and again in January 1885. In December 1886 the paper listed her among old-timers, at home in Mingusville.

moments.label: Visited friends in Medora

people.name: Mike Knott
people.bio: Mike (Michael) Knott kept a saloon in Medora, beside which John Doulisch was hurt while excavating in March 1884, and in April 1885 the paper, amid complaints about running vagrants out of town, joked that he should be made 'foreman of the stiff-firing gang.' In October 1886 he traded his store building for Tompkins' ranch down the river, planning to farm.

moments.label: Joked about as 'foreman of the stiff-firing gang'
Traded his building for a ranch down the river

people.name: Mrs. Arch Boyd
people.role: Wife of hotel man Arch Boyd
people.bio: Mrs. Arch Boyd was reported ill in December 1884 and September 1885 and helped her husband host a well-attended gathering at the Northern Pacific hotel at the end of 1885. In December 1886 the couple left Medora for Minot.

moments.label: Co-hosted a gathering at the Northern Pacific hotel
Left Medora with her husband for Minot

people.name: Mrs. D. K. Wade
people.role: Wife of rancher D. K. Wade
people.bio: Mrs. D. K. Wade lived with her husband at Tepee bottom, where a riding party from the paper called on them in July 1884, and where their young friend Miss Taylor of Boston came to spend the summer of 1885. In December 1886 she was visiting her mother in New Brighton, Pa.

moments.label: Her friend Miss Taylor came to spend the summer at Tepee bottom ranch

people.name: Mrs. J. D. Garver
people.bio: Mrs. J. D. Garver had a new baby in March 1885, according to a story the paper attributed to her son Georgie. At the end of March 1885 she took the children to Bismarck to visit her mother, and in April she fell ill there and her husband went down to care for her.

moments.label: Fell ill while visiting Bismarck

people.name: Mrs. M. M. Coleman
people.role: Wife of M. M. Coleman of Medora
people.bio: Mrs. M. M. Coleman and her husband celebrated their 18th wedding anniversary in February 1885. That June she was struck by a spasm that left her unconscious for several days, but she recovered.

moments.label: Recovered after days unconscious from a spasm

people.name: Mrs. Paddock
people.role: Medora woman who hosted visiting women
people.bio: Mrs. Paddock hosted visitors in Medora, including a Mrs. McGregor in 1885 and 1886 and, in August 1885, the sister of Bob Roberts, who had come with him from Wales. In April 1885 the paper announced a birth in the Paddock household.

moments.label: Birth announced in the Paddock household
Hosted Roberts' sister, newly arrived from Wales

people.match_note: Probably Mrs. E. G. Paddock, but a Mrs. Wm. Paddock also appears.

people.name: Nehemiah G. Ordway
people.bio: Nehemiah G. Ordway was governor of Dakota Territory, and the Cow Boy credited him in May 1884 with organizing Billings County, probably one of his last official acts before his term expired that summer. In July 1884 the paper criticized him for believing Gallien's stories about cowboys.

moments.label: Organized Billings County
Successor named as his term expired

people.name: Norman J. Colman
people.bio: As U.S. Commissioner of Agriculture (spelled Coleman in the paper), he appears in 1885 working to stamp out cattle disease in Missouri, questioning Texas cowmen with a view to easing the quarantine, and reading a paper at the National Cattle Growers' Association meeting in Chicago that November. In 1886 the paper reported he had sent botanist George Vasey to study the grasses of the arid West.

moments.label: Questioned Texas cowmen about the cattle quarantine
Read a paper to the National Cattle Growers

people.name: Paddy Ryan
people.role: Prizefighter, opponent of John L. Sullivan
people.bio: Paddy Ryan was a prizefighter whose rivalry with John L. Sullivan the Cow Boy followed, noting in 1885 that Medora's young men were practicing to challenge either and that the two had signed to fight at Butte City. In November 1886 the paper reported that Sullivan knocked Ryan out in the third round at San Francisco.

moments.label: Knocked out by Sullivan in third round at San Francisco

people.name: R. B. Harrison
people.role: Secretary of the Montana Stockgrowers' Association
people.bio: R. B. Harrison was secretary of the Montana Stockgrowers' Association, elected secretary and treasurer at its April 1885 meeting and calling the roll at its fall 1885 meeting in Helena. In November 1885 he passed through Medora with President Bryan and Granville Stuart on the way to the national association meeting.

moments.label: Called the roll at the stockgrowers' meeting

people.name: S. G. Smith
people.role: Superintendent of the Medora stage line
people.bio: S. G. Smith of Bismarck became superintendent of the stage company in February 1885. By December 1886 he was living at Menoken, Dakota.

moments.label: Named superintendent of the stage company

people.name: Schaefer
people.bio: Schaefer was a billiards champion whose matches with Slosson and Vignaux the Cow Boy followed in its sporting notes, including his loss to Slosson at Chicago in 1884. In December 1885 the paper reported that he had taken first prize in the world championship series.

moments.label: Lost to Slosson at balk-line billiards in Chicago
Won the world billiard championship

people.name: Seth Wyland
people.bio: Seth Wyland was a top shot in the Bad Lands Gun Club, leading the club's third shoot of March 1885 with 59. When he left for a winter hunting trip in October 1885, the club gave him the first prize.

moments.label: Led the gun club shoot with 59
Awarded the club's first prize

people.name: Sheriff Cuskelley
people.bio: Sheriff Cuskelley of Dickinson came west in 1884 to replevin a pony at Belfield, gather witnesses in Medora for the Moody-Malloy trial, and transport accused horse thieves. In late summer 1884 he went to the Standing Rock agency with Robert Milligan to recover horses stolen from Milligan at Sully Springs.

moments.label: Brought two accused horse thieves through Medora
Recovered stolen horses at Standing Rock agency

people.match_note: First name not given; may be Pat or Joe Cuskelley

people.name: Slosson
people.bio: Slosson was a billiards player whose matches the Cow Boy followed in its sporting notes, reporting in June 1884 that he beat the champion Schaefer at balk-line in Chicago. In December 1885 he finished third behind Schaefer and Vignaux in a series for the world billiard championship.

moments.label: Beat Schaefer at balk-line billiards in Chicago
Finished third in the world billiard championship

people.name: Smith
people.bio: Items under the bare name Smith refer to different men: Superintendent Smith of the stage road, who came in from the line in March 1885 and lost his post that April, deputy marshal Smith of Miles City, who arrested Win Roberts in May 1885, and a Smith of Germantown, Pennsylvania, visiting Howard Eaton's ranch in March 1886.

moments.label: Stage road superintendent came in from the line
Deputy marshal arrested Win Roberts

people.match_note: mixed contexts; partly the stage superintendent (S. G. Smith)

people.name: T. W. Ingersoll
people.bio: T. W. Ingersoll, a St. Paul photographer, stayed in Medora about ten days in September 1885, hunting and taking many photographic views of the Bad Lands. He later wrote that the views were turning out well and that ordered prints would be delivered through the Cow Boy office.

moments.label: Stopped in Medora on a photographing trip
Reported success with his Bad Lands views

people.name: Tommy Skinner
people.role: Medora cowhand; member of the Marquise's 1885 hunting party
people.bio: Tommy Skinner went with the Marquise de Mores' hunting party to the Big Horn country in July 1885 and brought the stock back to Medora. In February 1886 he went to the Cave Hills with Lloyd Roberts and fell sick at a camp on the return.

moments.label: Joined the Marquise's hunting party to the Big Horn
Fell sick returning from the Cave Hills

people.name: Towers
people.bio: Towers was a cattleman who came to town with Boice in March 1884 to arrange the April round-up meeting at Little Missouri, and in 1885 proposed a Wyoming association resolution barring horse racing on members' ranches. In April 1886 he attended the Little Missouri stockgrowers' meeting as one of the members from Mingusville.

moments.label: Arranged a round-up meeting with Boice
Proposed banning horse racing on association ranches

people.match_note: G. W. or W. A. Towers

people.name: W. A. Van Brunt
people.role: Wisconsin cattle company president visiting for the round-up
people.bio: W. A. Van Brunt of Wisconsin came out in May 1885 to spend about six weeks on the round-up and left pleased with his cattle. The paper calls him president of both the Badger cattle company and the VI cattle company.

moments.label: Left after six weeks on the round-up

people.match_note: Merged with 'W. A. VanBrunt' across shards.

people.name: W. B. Pryor
people.role: Medora boot, shoe and leather shop owner
people.bio: W. B. Pryor of Dickinson came to Medora in the spring of 1885 and built a new shop for boots, shoes and leather work, mending harness and saddles as well. By mid-April 1885 his business had opened and he was looking for a shoemaker.

moments.label: Opened his boot and shoe business

people.name: W. D. Smith
people.role: Montana stock inspector from Miles City
people.bio: W. D. Smith, a Montana stock inspector from Miles City, came to Medora in 1884 while pursuing thieves and looking into the Marquis' stolen ponies. In June 1885 he inspected the Hash Knife herd at Medora and was credited with catching his man at Rapid City.

moments.label: Pursued thieves and investigated the Marquis' stolen ponies
Inspected the Hash Knife herd at Medora

people.match_note: Wm. Smith (Montana cattle inspector, 1884) merged

people.name: A. H. Arnett
people.role: Partner in Arnett & Thomas, owners of the AHA brand
people.bio: A. H. Arnett was a partner in Arnett & Thomas, owners of the ΛHΛ brand, with a Dickinson post office, who published their brand in the Cow Boy in November 1885. He represented the brand at the April 1886 stockgrowers' meeting, and that May the firm added about 30 Hereford bulls to its herd.

moments.label: Added about 30 full-blood Hereford bulls to the herd

people.name: Al. Canter
people.role: Foreman of the Bad Lands Cattle Co.
people.bio: Al. Canter was foreman of the Bad Lands Cattle Co. In June 1885 he advertised a $10 reward for a rawhide lariat lost near the mouth of Box Elder.

moments.label: Offered $10 for a lost rawhide lariat

people.name: Al. Gifford
people.bio: Al. Gifford passed through Medora in 1884 and came down from Glendive in June 1885 saying he would settle in Medora if a South America plan fell through. By December 1886 the paper listed him among old-timers, married and living in Miles City.

moments.label: Weighed South America or settling in Medora

people.name: Alaska John
people.bio: Alaska John ran the 'Oyster Grotto' in Medora, where in January 1885 he put up a sign advertising fresh oysters 'blood raw, dead or alive.' A watch was raffled at his place in February 1885.

moments.label: Hung a new sign on the Oyster Grotto

people.name: Alex. McKenzie
people.bio: Alex. McKenzie of Bismarck was among those invited to accompany the first stage from Medora to Deadwood in October 1884, along with Governor Pierce, and he spent several days in Medora in December 1886. In March 1885 a resolution in the territorial council called for investigating charges of bribes offered by him and others.

moments.label: Named in council resolution on bribery charges

people.name: Alex. Metzger
people.bio: Alex. Metzger of Bismarck visited Medora in April, August and September 1884. The paper gives no other details about him.

moments.label: Visited Medora from Bismarck

people.name: Allen
people.bio: The name 'Allen' covers more than one man in these items. One Allen traveled the Medora route to Deadwood with Jones in April 1884 and a Superintendent Allen of the stage line left for the Hills in May 1885, while a General Allen of Fargo was mentioned as a possible nominee in 1886.

moments.label: Stage line superintendent left for the Hills

people.match_note: Contexts mix the Black Hills shippers (1884), a stage-line superintendent (1885) and a congressional candidate (1886)

people.name: Annie Brophy
people.role: Mingusville woman who married John Munro
people.bio: Annie Brophy of Mingusville visited Medora with her sister Mary in November 1884 and came down for a dance in March 1885. She married John Munro at the Catholic church in August 1885.

moments.label: Married John Munro at the Catholic church

people.name: Avery
people.bio: Avery of Augusta, Me., called at the Cow Boy office in February 1884 while the editor was away. In April 1884 the paper reported that a Mr. Avery, who had been visiting A. M. Sinnott for some time, had returned east.

moments.label: Called at the Cow Boy office

people.name: B. J. VanVleck
people.role: Mandan man; aided Billings County organization
people.bio: B. J. VanVleck of Mandan was named for register of deeds in October 1886. In November 1886 the Billings County commissioners paid him six dollars for services in organizing the county.

moments.label: Paid for services organizing Billings County

people.name: Baroness von Hoffman
people.bio: The Baroness von Hoffman and the Baron returned from a western trip in their special car on September 25, 1884. That month the paper corrected an earlier report about a new brick cottage she was building.

moments.label: Returned from a western trip in her special car

people.name: Benjamin Harrison
people.bio: The future president, then a U.S. senator from Indiana, appears in the Cow Boy as a possible 1884 Republican nominee and in July 1885 as chairman of the Senate Indian affairs committee visiting the Crow Creek and Winnebago reservations. In December 1885 he introduced a bill to admit part of Dakota as a state.

moments.label: Introduced a bill to admit southern Dakota

people.name: Birdie Wadsworth
people.role: Young woman named in the Medora local news
people.bio: Miss Birdie Wadsworth went to Bismarck to attend school in September 1885. In 1886 she visited friends in Steele and was sick for several days in December.

moments.label: Left for school in Bismarck

people.name: Bob Thompson
people.role: Bad Lands man accused of horse theft
people.bio: Bob Thompson left the Bad Lands in August 1886, and the paper first reported he had taken four of the best horses of the 13 outfit. In September the 13 camp reported no horses missing, so the paper withdrew the charge.

moments.label: Reported to have stolen four horses
Theft report contradicted by the 13 camp

people.name: C. A. Lounsberry
people.bio: Col. C. A. Lounsberry of Bismarck was endorsed by the Billings County Republican convention in April 1884 for a territorial office. In May 1884 he started the Bismarck Journal, which the Cow Boy welcomed.

moments.label: Launched the Bismarck Journal

people.name: C. D. Edick
people.bio: C. D. Edick of the Bismarck cigar makers Edick Bros. called on Medora's cigar dealers in April 1884, September 1884 and January 1885. On his first visit he reported numerous sales and was pleased with Medora's prospects.

moments.label: Reported good cigar sales in Medora

people.name: C. E. Finn
people.bio: C. E. Finn advertised as an artist in the Cow Boy in February 1884. By March he had moved his tent gallery to Miles City.

moments.label: Moved his tent gallery to Miles City

people.name: Charles Uderman
people.bio: Charles Uderman was nominated by acclamation for constable at the October 1886 citizens' nominating convention. He was listed among the successful candidates in November 1886.

moments.label: Listed among the successful constable candidates

people.name: Cold Turkey Bill
people.role: Stage-line hand at North Grand station
people.bio: "Cold Turkey Bill" came into Medora from the North Grand stage station in March 1885 and was teased by the paper for dressing up. By March 1886 he was reported in Billings, Montana.

moments.label: Came in from North Grand stage station

people.name: Cole
people.bio: The name Cole appears for a Montana cattleman from Miles City who visited in July 1884, and in 1885 for a "Bro. Cole" who, the paper joked, would now have a force pump by the company's office for watering trees in "the Park" and a "His Honor Cole" who got soaked crossing Sully creek. The excerpts do not show whether these are the same man.

moments.label: Montana cattleman Cole visited from Miles City

people.name: Colonel Malone
people.role: Stock agent of the Chicago, Milwaukee & St. Paul railway
people.bio: Colonel Malone was the stock agent of the Chicago, Milwaukee & St. Paul railway. He passed through Medora in 1885 and 1886.

moments.label: Passed through en route to Chicago

people.name: Cornelis VanEeghen
people.role: Brother of J. A. VanEeghen, visiting from Amsterdam
people.bio: Cornelis VanEeghen, brother of J. A. VanEeghen, visited the Garner Creek horse ranch in September 1885. He left that month for his home in Amsterdam, Holland, much pleased with the Bad Lands.

moments.label: Left for his home in Amsterdam

people.name: Dan Eisenberg
people.bio: Dan Eisenberg was a Bismarck merchant whose traveling salesmen, Will McNaughton and Lee Eisenberg, took orders in Medora during 1884. The paper reported that his house did considerable business in town.

moments.label: His salesman did brisk business in Medora

people.name: Dave Brown
people.bio: Dave Brown of Mingusville was quoted in an April 1886 item on mavericks as saying that ropes came high but he must have them at any price. In May 1886 he and his wife accompanied the newly married Mr. and Mrs. Jack Tisdale to Medora.

moments.label: Quoted on the high price of ropes

people.name: Dr. W. H. Williamson
people.bio: Dr. W. H. Williamson, a Bismarck dentist, announced a week of dental work at Medora's Northern Pacific hotel beginning April 10, 1886, at Howard Eaton's request. In May 1886 the Cow Boy denounced a Bismarck telegram claiming that revolvers were fired all night at a cowboy ball in the hotel and that his door was riddled; the paper said a single shot had been fired in the hall outside his room and blamed him for carrying a highly colored account to Bismarck.

moments.label: Announced a week of dental work in Medora
Blamed for an exaggerated report of a shooting

people.name: Duryea
people.role: Surveyor working along the Little Missouri, 1884
people.bio: Duryea led a surveying party down the Little Missouri in 1884. The paper calls him both a Northern Pacific surveyor and a member of the government surveying party.

moments.label: His surveying party worked down the river

people.name: E. Kessler
people.bio: E. Kessler of New York spent a month hunting at Jack McGregor's ranch in fall 1885 and took several fine heads. While hunting below the mouth of Beaver Creek with Tommy McGregor, he came upon two bears feeding.

moments.label: Came upon two bears while hunting

people.name: E. W. Caldwell
people.bio: E. W. Caldwell, auditor of Dakota Territory, certified the Fargo Insurance Company's annual statement printed in the Cow Boy in February 1886. His name also appeared as auditor on a March 1886 communication.

moments.label: Certified Fargo Insurance Company annual statement

people.name: Ed. Gallien
people.bio: Ed. Gallien of Belfield went east with his family in early 1884 after his father's death and was held up in St. Paul on the way back by his daughter's illness. In April 1884 he proved up on his homestead, the third proved up at Belfield in four months.

moments.label: Proved up on his Belfield homestead

people.name: F. E. Bowen
people.bio: F. E. Bowen was a rising Mandan attorney who did business in Medora in October 1884. In October 1886 he was named for district attorney.

moments.label: Visited Medora on legal business

people.name: F. W. McKinney
people.bio: F. W. (Fred) McKinney of Bismarck visited Medora in 1884 with an officer of the Refrigerator Car Co. He stopped over again in April 1885.

moments.label: Visited Medora with Refrigerator Car Co. party

people.name: Father Cassidy
people.role: Catholic priest from Mandan, later of Jamestown
people.bio: Father Cassidy of Mandan visited George Fitzgerald in April 1884 and in May said mass in Medora, planning to return every two or three weeks. By July 1884 Father Martin had taken his place at Mandan and he had charge of the Jamestown parish.

moments.label: Held mass in Medora

people.name: Ferris
people.bio: A Mr. Ferris was a pall-bearer at a ranch funeral in October 1885 and represented the 13 outfit at the stockgrowers' meeting in April 1886. In September 1886 he was to accompany the river outfits' beef cattle to market.

moments.label: Represented the 13 outfit at the stockgrowers' meeting

people.match_note: Sylvane or Joe Ferris

people.name: Field
people.role: Dakota sub-commissioner to the New Orleans world's fair
people.bio: Mr. Field, sub-commissioner of Dakota to the New Orleans world's fair, was in Medora in October 1884 collecting specimens and curiosities for the exposition. In August 1884 the Cow Boy reprinted a Livingston Enterprise report that twenty horses had disappeared from a Mr. Field's herd.

moments.label: Collected Bad Lands specimens for New Orleans

people.match_note: a Livingston horse owner and J. A. Field, Dakota sub-commissioner to New Orleans fair

people.name: Fitzgerald
people.bio: The name Fitzgerald appears for a pedestrian who walked 610 miles in a six-day match in New York in 1884, and for the owner of Fitzgerald's hotel in Medora in 1886. These are different people.

moments.label: Fitzgerald's hotel named in a Medora fire warning

people.name: Ford
people.role: Helena freighter with a mule outfit
people.bio: Ford ran a freighting outfit of twenty wagons and seventy-five mules that came from Helena to Medora in June 1884. In July he took loads at Belfield for $1.50 rather than stand idle.

moments.label: Freighting outfit reported on its way from Helena
Accepted $1.50 rate for freighting from Belfield

people.name: Frank Coughlan
people.bio: Frank Coughlan was Medora's postmaster in early 1884, and in February he left for a camp forty miles down the river. In March 1884 he left for New York, saying he would return as soon as possible.

moments.label: Left for New York

people.name: Frank Wadsworth
people.role: Stockman fatally shot by accident at Wadsworth's line camp
people.bio: Frank Wadsworth was badly wounded in May 1885 at Wadsworth's line camp at the head of Frank's Creek, when a gun in Joe Graham's hands went off accidentally. He died a few days later, and the paper wrote that few deaths were so widely mourned.

moments.label: Died of an accidental gunshot wound

people.name: G. H. Spear
people.role: Spearfish man running stages to Deadwood
people.bio: G. H. Spear of Spearfish set out for Deadwood in May 1884. In July 1884 the editor rode to Deadwood in one of Mr. Spear's stages, and the paper cited Spear as praising the Medora freight route.

moments.label: Editor rode to Deadwood in his stage

people.name: Geo. Wilder
people.role: Iowa visitor traveling to the Black Hills
people.bio: George Wilder and his wife, of Iowa, passed through Medora for the Black Hills in July 1885. They came back in August 1885 with John Beers.
