people.name: Grantier
people.bio: Grantier was the Northern Pacific's carpenter foreman at Medora, and in August 1884 he built a large platform and derrick at the new warehouse for Black Hills freight. In September 1884 he finished an office and baggage room there for the Medora Stage and Forwarding company.

moments.label: Completed office for the Medora Stage and Forwarding company

people.name: Gustave Stoltze
people.bio: Gustave Stoltze was a draughtsman for the N. P. R. C. Co. when he visited Medora in February 1884. In July 1884, when he was in town again, the paper called him the company's architect.

moments.label: Visited Medora as the company's architect

people.name: H. A. Sprague
people.role: Black Hills member of the territorial legislature
people.bio: H. A. Sprague was one of the Black Hills members of the territorial legislature credited by the Cow Boy with passing the fence law and repealing the herd law in March 1885. That month he passed through Medora on his way home from Bismarck to the Hills.

moments.label: Credited with helping pass the fence law

people.name: H. Gilbert
people.bio: H. Gilbert took part in the April 1884 Republican county convention. In August 1885 he wrote from Sentinel Butte that some of his cattle had died, and investigation pointed to dry murrain.

moments.label: Reported cattle deaths at Sentinel Butte

people.name: H. M. Heath
people.role: Wells, Fargo & Co. express route agent
people.bio: H. M. Heath was the travelling route agent of Wells, Fargo & Co.'s express, who in December 1884 came to Medora to set up agent Maxwell as agent for two rival express companies. In January 1885 the paper joked about his friendly meeting with DeForce, the rival company's route agent.

moments.label: Set up Maxwell as agent for two express companies

people.name: H. R. Lyon
people.role: Mandan man favored for the legislature in 1886
people.bio: H. R. Lyon of Mandan was the Cow Boy's preferred candidate for the legislature in August and September 1886, and the delegates from its area favored him. In October 1886 Mitchell of Mandan won the Morton County delegates after a sharp contest, but the paper said the legislative nomination was still open between the two.

moments.label: Lost the Morton County delegates to Mitchell

people.name: Harry Barker
people.bio: Harry Barker took Geo. Wilkes' place as engineer at the slaughter-house in August 1885. A year later he married Lena Eager at Dickinson and settled at the Cantonment.

moments.label: Became engineer at the slaughter-house
Married Lena Eager at Dickinson

people.name: Harry Bennett
people.role: Cowhand who drove horses and cattle
people.bio: Harry Bennett returned in June 1886 after recovering eight of Johnny Goodall's horses about sixty miles west of Fort McGinness, and brought back a story of lariat skill. In October 1886 he started out with Ferris & Merrifield's cattle, planning to winter at his home in Ohio.

moments.label: Recovered Goodall's horses west of Fort McGinness
Left with Ferris & Merrifield's cattle

people.name: Hattie Eaton
people.bio: Miss Hattie Eaton, sister of the Eaton brothers, came with her parents in April 1885 to spend the summer at the logging camp. She returned to the Bad Lands for the summer of 1886.

moments.label: Arrived to spend the summer at the logging camp

people.name: Henry M. Teller
people.bio: Henry M. Teller, Secretary of the Interior, appeared in the Cow Boy in March 1884 as the official cattlemen petitioned to keep open a cattle trail from Texas, and in January 1885 as the secretary a congressional committee asked for details of land leases. In June 1885 the paper printed a reply from a "Sec'y. Teller" on taxes levied on Billings County by Morton and Stark counties.

moments.label: Cattlemen petitioned him on the Texas cattle trail

people.name: Henry Scott
people.role: Accused horse thief, partner of Clay Layton
people.bio: Henry Scott, called 'Scotty,' was arrested in August 1884 at Dixon's ranch and, with Clay Layton, was charged with stealing four horses from Archie Morton of South Heart; the two passed through Medora in the Dickinson sheriff's custody. In September 1884 the two escaped from the Dickinson jail.

moments.label: Arrested for stealing four horses
Escaped from the Dickinson jail

people.name: Henry Williams
people.bio: Henry Williams, a cowboy working for Gregor Lang, won a steer-roping prize at the June 1886 round-up, and in July a Henry Williams of the Neimmella cattle company set a roping record. In December 1886 a warrant was issued for his arrest as an accessory in the case against George Myers.

moments.label: Won a roping prize at the round-up
Warrant issued as accessory in the George Myers case

people.name: Herbert D. Hostetter
people.role: Pittsburgh visitor at Howard Eaton's ranch
people.bio: Herbert D. Hostetter of Pittsburgh made yearly visits to Howard Eaton's ranch, staying several weeks in 1884 and again in the fall of 1885. In October 1885 he cut his foot and went to Glendive for medical care.

moments.label: Cut his foot and went to Glendive for care

people.match_note: D. H. Hostetter (1884) assumed same annual visitor

people.name: Ira C. Bellows
people.role: Mandan man; plaintiff in a Morton County court case
people.bio: Ira C. Bellows of Mandan visited Medora in June 1884. In September 1885 he and James Bellows were listed as plaintiffs in a Morton County district court case.

moments.label: Named plaintiff in a Morton County court case

people.name: J. H. Kelly
people.role: Telegraph operator at Medora, then Dickinson
people.bio: J. H. Kelly of Duluth took over Medora's telegraph office in September 1884. In November 1884 he moved to the operator's job at Dickinson.

moments.label: Took over the Medora telegraph office
Transferred to Dickinson

people.name: J. H. Lander
people.bio: J. H. Lander was named as a foreman in the round-up district lists the paper printed in spring 1885. The notices ran from April into May 1885.

moments.label: Named foreman in the round-up district list

people.name: J. Hayes Moore
people.role: Rancher in the Killdeer Mountains country
people.bio: J. Hayes Moore had what the paper called a first-rate ranch in the Killdeer Mountains country in 1884. In October 1885 the Cow Boy reported his death from concussion of the brain after an accident, which recalled his mother, Lydia A. Moore, from Minneapolis.

moments.label: Death reported, from concussion of the brain

people.name: J. J. Fitzgerald
people.bio: J. J. Fitzgerald kept a restaurant in Medora in early 1884 and that May finished clearing the bottom below the Marquis' residence. In December 1884 he sent his wife and family to Iowa for the winter.

moments.label: Cleared the bottom below the Marquis' residence
Sent his family to Iowa for the winter

people.name: J. R. Fegan
people.role: Acting Northern Pacific station agent at Medora, 1884
people.bio: J. R. Fegan served as acting station agent at Medora in October 1884 while agent Brinker was on leave. In November 1884 he exchanged places with Mr. Maxwell of the car accountant's office in Mandan.

moments.label: Became acting agent during Brinker's leave

people.name: J. R. Widmyer
people.bio: J. R. Widmyer of the Glendive Independent visited the Cow Boy in September 1884, and in February 1886 the paper mocked the poetry in his paper's railroad column. In April 1886 he attended the Little Missouri stockgrowers' meeting with other newspapermen.

moments.label: Attended the stockgrowers' meeting as a newspaperman

people.name: J. W. Reynolds
people.bio: J. W. Reynolds was the Cow Boy's printer and signed the Republican convention call of April 1884. He left for the East in May 1884 with the editor's praise.

moments.label: Left Medora; praised as a top Dakota printer

people.name: Jack Matlock
people.bio: Jack Matlock wrote to the Cow Boy in November 1885 from Lavina, Montana, where he drove on the Billings and Fort Benton stage line, and was still on that line in March 1886. By August 1886 he was driving for the National Park stage line.

moments.label: Driving the Billings-Fort Benton stage line
Driving for the National Park stage line

people.name: James G. Blaine
people.bio: The Republican presidential nominee of 1884 appears in the Cow Boy during that spring's race for the nomination, when he and President Arthur were leading. In June 1884 the paper predicted that Blaine and Logan would be elected.

moments.label: Paper predicted Blaine and Logan would win

people.name: James Harmon
people.bio: James 'Jim' Harmon was thrown by a bronco in September 1885 and badly sprained his ankle, and he bid on stock at a sale that fall. In October 1885 his wife returned from Minnesota with a new baby girl.

moments.label: Wife returned home with a new baby girl

people.name: Janie Fitzgerald
people.role: Medora young woman who died in 1885
people.bio: Janie Fitzgerald left Medora with Mrs. Fitzgerald in July 1885 for McGregor, Iowa, for her health. Word of improvement came that month, but on July 30, 1885, the paper reported her death.

moments.label: Left for McGregor, Iowa, for her health
Death reported

people.name: Jay Gould
people.bio: Jay Gould, the New York railroad financier, was mentioned in national news about Union Pacific debts in 1884. In December 1885 the paper reported he would quit stock speculation and turn his business over to his son.

moments.label: Reported quitting stock speculation

people.match_note: one context is a local joke

people.name: Jennie Macbeth
people.role: Mankato, Minn. woman who married W. H. Merrifield
people.bio: Jennie Macbeth of Mankato, Minnesota, visited Mrs. Wadsworth at the ranch in fall 1885 and went home to Mankato in December. In February 1886 the paper announced her wedding to W. H. Merrifield.

moments.label: Married W. H. Merrifield

people.match_note: Miss Macbeth merged on Wadsworth-ranch visit timing

people.name: Jimmy Emmons
people.bio: Jimmy Emmons edited the Dakota Blade, which in late 1884 and early 1885 argued against repealing the herd law in the Bad Lands. The Cow Boy answered that he had never been in the Bad Lands and that no one there had petitioned for repeal.

moments.label: Cow Boy rebutted his Dakota Blade herd-law argument

people.name: John Beers
people.role: Medora man who left with Wright as the Cantonment was attached
people.bio: John Beers escorted George Wilder and his wife of Iowa to the Black Hills in summer 1885. In October 1885 he and Wright left Medora, Beers for a railroad job in Butte, after turning the Cantonment over to the sheriff to satisfy attachments.

moments.label: Left with the Wilders for the Black Hills
Left for Butte; Cantonment turned over to sheriff

people.name: John Bozeman
people.role: Montana trail guide in J. S. Warn's Lost Cabin memoir
people.bio: John Bozeman appears in J. S. Warn's serialized memoir 'The Lost Cabin Gold Mines,' printed in summer 1885. Warn recalled him coming from Virginia City, Mont., to guide a wagon train on a short cut to the Alder Gulch mines, and later finding his camp on the Big Horn River.

moments.label: Recalled guiding emigrants toward Alder Gulch

people.name: John Munroe
people.role: Partner in Shaffer & Munroe, Plum Grove ranch
people.bio: John Munroe was a partner with Chas. Shaffer in Shaffer & Munroe, of the Plum Grove ranch on the Little Missouri. The partnership dissolved on May 24, 1884, and Munroe took on its debts.

moments.label: Dissolved partnership in the Plum Grove ranch

people.name: John Peehn
people.role: Billings County homesteader whose entry was contested
people.bio: John Peehn held a homestead entry dated April 9, 1883, in Billings County, which John Weber contested at the Bismarck land office in July 1884 for abandonment. The contest notice, summoning both men to a hearing on August 21, 1884, ran in the Cow Boy that summer.

moments.label: Homestead entry contested for abandonment

people.name: John R. Thayer
people.bio: John R. Thayer was a Belfield man mentioned in the town's gossip columns in March 1884. In July 1884 he left for the east, and the column said many expected him to return with a wife.

moments.label: Left Belfield for the east

people.name: John Sawyer
people.role: Bad Lands cowhand from Oak Bay, New Brunswick
people.bio: John Sawyer was named at the Little Missouri River Stockmen's Association meeting in April 1885 and dislocated his shoulder that October. In October 1886 he left for a winter at his old home in Oak Bay, New Brunswick, and the paper called him too good a cowpuncher to lose.

moments.label: Left for a winter visit to New Brunswick

people.match_note: John/Johnny merged on nickname

people.name: Jos. Doulisch
people.role: Laborer fatally injured in a foundation cave-in at Medora
people.bio: Jos. Doulisch was badly hurt in March 1884 when earth fell on him while he was excavating next to Michael Knott's saloon for a new building. He seemed to be recovering, but the paper reported his death in early April 1884.

moments.label: Injured in a cave-in while excavating
Died of his injuries

people.match_note: printed John in first report, Jos. thereafter

people.name: Joseph Hanauer
people.role: Glendive businessman; partner in Martindale & Hanauer
people.bio: Joseph Hanauer was a partner in the store of Martindale & Hanauer, which the paper said was doing a big business in August 1884. He came from Glendive to Medora on business in September 1885 and to visit in May 1886.

moments.label: Martindale & Hanauer store reported doing brisk trade

people.match_note: Bare 'Hanauer' (Belfield store) assumed to be the Glendive man

people.name: Julia Lason
people.bio: Mrs. Julia Lason was seriously ill in April 1885 but expected to recover. In June 1885 Patrick O'Hara of the Medora Coal Co. bought her house in Little Missouri to move to Medora.

moments.label: Sold her Little Missouri house to Patrick O'Hara

people.name: Lamb
people.role: Partner in Lamb & Holland, Boston cattlemen
people.bio: Lamb, of the Boston firm Lamb & Holland, bought Billy Paddock's ranch down the river in March 1885 to stock with cattle.

moments.label: Firm bought Billy Paddock's ranch

people.match_note: Mostly B. F. Lamb (Lamb & Holland), but also a Lamb of Mankato

people.name: Lee Eisenberg
people.role: Traveling dry goods salesman for Dan Eisenberg, Bismarck
people.bio: Lee Eisenberg traveled for the Bismarck dry goods house of Dan Eisenberg and took orders in Medora in May and October 1884. He came again with a line of dry goods in April 1885.

moments.label: Did considerable business in Medora for Dan Eisenberg

people.name: Lincoln Lee
people.role: Bad Lands bronco buster; convicted cattle thief
people.bio: Lincoln "Link" Lee was known in the Bad Lands as a fine bronco buster, and in July 1885 a Lincoln Lee opened court as sheriff in Justice Gordon's court. After leaving for Montana in 1885 he was jailed for illegally branding cattle on the Rosebud, and in November 1886 he was in the Deer Lodge penitentiary.

moments.label: Jailed in Montana for illegal branding

people.name: Link Gates
people.bio: Link Gates killed a mountain sheep with Howard Eaton in September 1885 and bid on stock at a sale that fall. In a roping contest at Pierre Wibaux's ranch in June 1886 he placed second after his rope broke.

moments.label: Placed second in roping contest after rope broke

people.name: M. D. Auld
people.bio: M. D. Auld headed M. D. Auld & Co. of Belfield, which ran a 'For Sale Cheap' advertisement in the Cow Boy in spring 1886 offering a hay press for $275.

moments.label: Advertised goods for sale cheap

people.name: Mary Coleman
people.role: Medora woman married at the Catholic church in 1885
people.bio: Mollie Coleman traveled to Andrews station and Sentinel Butte in summer 1884. In August 1885 Mary, eldest daughter of a Mr. and Mrs. Coleman, was married at the Catholic church in Medora by Father Martin.

moments.label: Married at Medora's Catholic church

people.match_note: Mollie taken as Mary

people.name: Matthews
people.bio: The name Matthews appears for the owner of a camp where horses were stolen in February 1884, for a stock inspector in town in October 1884, and for the man Tuttle defeated for sheriff at Glendive in November 1886.

moments.label: Lost the Glendive sheriff race to Tuttle

people.match_note: mixes Matthews' camp, Stock Inspector Matthews and 1886 election returns

people.name: Miller
people.bio: The surname Miller covers unrelated people in the Cow Boy: Miller of the California cattle firm Miller & Lux, a Cleveland visitor looking for a ranch site in June 1885, and a man named with Moore as facing trial in the Luffsey killing in September 1885. No single bio can be written from these items.

moments.label: Named as facing trial in the Luffsey killing

people.match_note: mixes Miller & Lux, a Cleveland cattle investor and the Luffsey case

people.name: Miss Friedman
people.role: Summer 1884 visitor at the Sloping Bottom ranch
people.bio: Miss Friedman spent part of summer 1884 visiting the Sloping Bottom ranch and attended local gatherings with the Roberts family. She left for Mandan in early August 1884.

moments.label: Left for Mandan after a ranch visit

people.name: Mr. Gallup
people.role: New York lawyer visiting the Bad Lands, July 1884
people.bio: Mr. Gallup of the New York law firm Johnson, Gallup & Hurry came through from the Black Hills in July 1884 and stayed at Wadsworth's ranch during calf branding. The paper reported he left convinced the Bad Lands would become one of the country's great cattle sections.

moments.label: Left convinced of the Bad Lands' cattle future

people.match_note: possibly the later Cave Hills Gallup; kept apart

people.name: Mr. Rowe
people.role: Cattleman of Rowe, Parker & Easton; Billings County commissioner
people.bio: Mr. Rowe of Rowe, Parker & Easton was listed among the cattlemen in April 1885 and proposed for county commissioner in October 1885. In December 1886 the paper urged him, as the third commissioner, to qualify at once.

moments.label: Proposed for county commissioner
Urged to qualify as third commissioner

people.match_note: Could be D. C. or Chas. Rowe.

people.name: Mrs. F. H. Ertel
people.role: Wife of Fred Ertel of Belfield
people.bio: Mrs. Fred Ertel of Belfield hosted the editor and joined social gatherings in 1884. In August 1884 she left Belfield with her children for St. Louis.

moments.label: Left Belfield with her children for St. Louis

people.name: Mrs. J. L. Truscott
people.role: Wife of J. L. Truscott (née Maggie Gardient)
people.bio: Mrs. J. L. Truscott, née Maggie Gardient, arrived in Medora in July 1885 and first stayed at the Northern Pacific. By early 1886 the Truscotts were living at the Spring Creek ranch.

moments.label: Arrived in Medora as Mrs. Truscott

people.name: Mrs. M. Wadsworth
people.bio: Mrs. Wadsworth served dinner to the editor's party at Wadsworth's ranch in late June 1884, and the paper called her the most hospitable of ladies. In October 1885 Miss Macbeth visited her at the ranch.

moments.label: Hosted the editor's party at Wadsworth's ranch

people.name: Mrs. Sewall
people.bio: Mrs. Sewall arrived from Maine in August 1885 with Wilmot Dow and his wife and settled at the Elkhorn ranch. Later that month she and Mrs. Dow joined their husbands in welcoming a Bad Lands excursion party there.

moments.label: Arrived from Maine for the Elkhorn ranch
Welcomed an excursion party at Elkhorn

people.name: Neil Gilmour
people.role: Receiver of the Bismarck land office
people.bio: Neil Gilmour was receiver of the Bismarck land office. He visited Medora in June 1885 and again in October 1885.

moments.label: Visited Medora as receiver of the land office

people.name: Nitch
people.bio: Nitch was a Bad Lands local named in the paper's joking social notes, listed among the 'bloods' in town in February 1884. In March 1885 the paper reported that he had 'buried the hatchet' and sworn off temptation.

moments.label: Announced he had buried the hatchet

people.name: Norman G. Dakin
people.bio: Norman G. Dakin of LaPorte, Indiana, a boyhood friend of the editor, called at the Cow Boy in May 1885 on his way back from Portland, Oregon, and reported stock looking well along the line. He called again in August and November 1885.

moments.label: Called at the Cow Boy returning from Oregon

people.name: O. H. Holt
people.role: Private secretary to Governor Pierce; writer on Dakota
people.bio: O. H. Holt of Bismarck, private secretary to Governor Pierce, published a pamphlet on Dakota's resources in 1885. The paper praised it, though it quoted the editor's early mistake about cattle pawing through snow.

moments.label: Published a pamphlet on Dakota's resources

people.name: P. D. O'Brien
people.bio: P. D. O'Brien, a Deadwood mining broker, came through Medora on the first coach from the Hills in October 1884, bound for Chicago and the east. He passed through again with his wife in January 1885.

moments.label: Came through on the first coach, bound east

people.name: Pat Donan
people.bio: Pat Donan was a Dakota booster whose glowing claims the Cow Boy rejected in 1884, and when he was mentioned for governor that June the paper denounced the idea. In January 1886 it named "Col. Pat. Donan" as part of a syndicate advertising a venture and warned the account would be flowery.

moments.label: Paper denounced talk of him as governor

people.name: Perfecto Fernandez
people.bio: Perfecto Fernandez, described by the paper as Mexican, came to the Bad Lands with Johnny Goodall in May 1884 and impressed the town by riding a horse that had thrown several others. He was in from Beaver creek in February 1885, and in April 1886 rode Gus Grisy's sorrel to victory in a horse race.

moments.label: Rode a bucking horse that had thrown others
Rode Gus Grisy's sorrel to a race win

people.name: Peter Fraser
people.bio: Peter Fraser (also Frazer or Frazier) opened his bar in Medora in April 1886. In June he left for Rapid City with others, and in July his wife left to join him there.

moments.label: Opened his bar in Medora

people.name: Peter Pelissier
people.bio: Peter Pelissier was nominated for constable at the Citizens' Nominating Convention in October 1886. The paper listed him among the successful candidates in November 1886.

moments.label: Elected constable

people.name: Pettigrew
people.role: Member of the Dakota territorial council
people.bio: Pettigrew sat in the Dakota territorial council in 1885, serving on the rules committee. The paper of March 12, 1885 reported that he argued for calling Steele before a council committee, and that in the capital debate a mock amendment drew laughter at his expense before he moved the previous question.

moments.label: Named to the council's rules committee

people.name: Phil Armour
people.role: Chicago meat packer and cattle buyer
people.bio: Phil Armour was a Chicago cattle buyer and meat packer; in February 1885 the paper reported one of the highest prices it had heard of, which he paid for steers, and in 1886 a Chicago commission man, speaking to Texas stockmen, called him virtually the only buyer on the Chicago market. In October 1886 the paper reported the end of the Chicago stockyards strike and the departure of the new men Armour had hired.

moments.label: Accused of controlling Chicago cattle prices

people.name: Pierce Boland
people.bio: In May 1885 Pierce Boland brought word that Dr. Robarts had successfully amputated an injured man's leg. In March 1886 he went to Helena.

moments.label: Brought news of a successful amputation

people.name: Piper
people.role: Bad Lands Gun Club rifle shooter
people.bio: Piper competed in the Bad Lands Gun Club's rifle shoots in early 1885. He scored 50 and 48 in two shoots reported in March 1885.

moments.label: Scored 50 in the gun club shoot

people.name: Prof. Wellung
people.role: Traveling magician at the Medora rink, July 1885
people.bio: Prof. Wellung gave a magic and variety entertainment at the Medora rink on the Fourth of July, 1885. Two weeks later the paper mocked the show as a fraud on a trusting public.

moments.label: Paper ridiculed his magic show

people.name: R. G. Head
people.role: Prairie Cattle Co. manager; president of the International Range Association
people.bio: R. G. Head, general manager of the Prairie Cattle Co., drew notice in May 1885 for a circular urging his cowboys to be gentlemen whatever their dress. By December 1886 he signed as president of the International Range Association.

moments.label: Issued a circular on cowboy manners
Signed as president of the International Range Association

people.name: R. H. Fulton
people.bio: R. H. Fulton held services in the Belfield Presbyterian church in April 1884, and the Belfield column hoped he would stay permanently. In May 1884 he reported four horses stolen at Belfield, and by July he was building a new cottage there.

moments.label: Held services in Belfield Presbyterian church

people.name: R. J. Jewell
people.bio: R. J. Jewell returned from an eastern trip in May 1884, still undecided about his future occupation. In July 1884 he was named in an item about plants with double and triple heads eighteen inches long.

moments.label: Returned from an eastern trip

people.name: Richard Gray
people.role: Agent of the N. P. Refrigerator Car Co.
people.bio: Richard Gray represented the company's interests at Fargo and visited Medora in February 1884. In November 1884 an R. Gray, agent for the N. P. R. C. Co. at Helena, spent a Sunday in Medora.

moments.label: Visited Medora on company business

people.name: Robert Nugent
people.bio: Robert Nugent lost three horses to lightning in August 1886, and three more of his horses went with J. A. VanEeghen's car shipment to St. Cloud. In October 1886 he and Moses Rider were expected back from a trip to St. Cloud.

moments.label: Three of his horses killed by lightning

people.name: S. M. Wills
people.bio: S. M. Wills of Mingusville bought saddle horses from John Goodall in June 1885. In April 1886 his gray horse won a 300-yard race against Pierre Wibaux's dun after Wibaux's rider fell off.

moments.label: His gray beat Pierre Wibaux's dun in a race

people.name: S. W. Russel
people.role: Book-keeper of the Niobrara Cattle Co., of Miles City
people.bio: S. W. Russel of Miles City, book-keeper of the Niobrara Cattle Co., delivered the company's N bar cattle and returned to Miles City in early August 1885. Later that month he delivered four hundred of the company's cattle, averaging 1,298½ pounds, to the Northern Pacific Refrigerator Car Co.

moments.label: Delivered four hundred Niobrara Co. cattle

people.name: Samuel McMaster
people.role: Homestake mine superintendent; 1884 candidate for delegate
people.bio: Samuel McMaster was superintendent at the Homestake mine, where the editor toured the stamp mills in 1884. In September 1884 he was a Black Hills candidate for delegate to Congress at the Pierre convention.

moments.label: Pressed for delegate at the Pierre convention

people.name: Sankey
people.role: Medora cowboy and rope artist, partner of Moody
people.bio: Sankey, half of the cowboy pair the paper called "Moody and Sankey" or "the gospel firm," left Medora in May 1884 with a Wild West outfit of cowboys, Crow Indians and broncos to perform in the east. He returned with Moody in August 1884, when the paper called them two of the best known cowboys around and unmatched with the lariat.

moments.label: Left with a Wild West show heading east
Returned to Medora from the Rocky Mountain show

people.name: Senator Vest
people.bio: A dispatch printed in January 1885 reported that Senator Vest had laid charges of fraud in the leasing of Indian lands to cattlemen before the Senate committee on Indian affairs. The Cow Boy attacked him and Senator Cockrell that month as hypocrites for opposing Dakota's admission on partisan grounds.

moments.label: Submitted charges of fraud in leases
Criticized for opposing Dakota's admission

people.name: Shorty
people.bio: A man called 'Shorty,' described by the paper as a handler of buffalo horns, lost the fat men's race at Medora's Fourth of July sports in 1885. In July 1886 he returned with Frank Foster's crew of butchers as one of the previous year's men.

moments.label: Lost the fat men's race on the Fourth
Returned with Frank Foster's butchers

people.name: Sidney Tarbell
people.bio: Sidney Tarbell was named to a committee at a Mingusville stockmen's meeting on March 31, 1886 and elected foreman of round-up No. 7. In May 1886 he was listed as foreman of District No. 7.

moments.label: Listed as round-up district foreman

people.name: Thomas McClung
people.role: Builder of Medora's billiard hall; later Dawson County deputy sheriff
people.bio: Thomas McClung won the contract to build Medora's new billiard hall in April 1884. By April 1885 he was serving as deputy sheriff of Dawson County, Montana.

moments.label: Won the contract for the new billiard hall
Serving as Dawson County deputy sheriff

people.name: Tom Martin
people.role: Sully creek man; later came from Bozeman
people.bio: Tom Martin hosted Mr. Gordon to dinner at Sully creek at the end of May 1885. In October 1886 he came from Bozeman to winter in the Bad Lands.

moments.label: Hosted Gordon at Sully creek
Came from Bozeman to winter in the Bad Lands

people.match_note: Tom/Tommy merged; one 1884 Tom Martin item is a Montana clipping

people.name: Tom Stack
people.bio: Tom Stack went to Belfield with Joe Pennell and Gill Kennedy in February 1884. In June 1884 the paper reported that Tobin of Mandan was considering a business partnership with him.

moments.label: Considered for a partnership by Tobin of Mandan

people.name: W. A. Towers
people.role: Partner in Towers & Gudgell, Colorado and Montana ranchmen
people.bio: W. A. Towers was a partner in Towers & Gudgell, Colorado and Montana ranchmen, and in August 1884 the paper reported his marriage at Decatur, Georgia, to Miss Fannie Hillyer. In May 1885, at a convention on the new cattle trail, he was the one conference committee member who did not sign a report favoring the trail, explaining his position as following his association's instructions.

moments.label: Married Fannie Hillyer at Decatur, Georgia

people.name: W. Aug. Fonda
people.bio: Major W. Aug. Fonda opened a law practice in Medora in June 1884 and became known for his puns. In January 1886 he was named postmaster at Stanton, the Mercer County seat.

moments.label: Began practicing law in Medora
Commissioned postmaster at Stanton

people.name: W. B. Milne
people.role: Minneapolis dry-goods salesman (Wyman, Mullin & Van Dyke)
people.bio: W. B. Milne was a travelling salesman for the Minneapolis dry-goods house of Wyman, Mullin & Van Dyke who made periodic visits to Medora from March 1884. By January 1885 the paper said he was doing a good business in Medora for his house and called him one of the most popular travelling men on the road.

moments.label: Praised as a popular travelling salesman

people.name: W. C. Cranston
people.bio: W. C. Cranston, called "the Blonde butcher," worked in Medora in summer 1885 and fought glove contests with a man named Ware in Chicago, losing by knockout in the second round in March 1886. In July 1886 he returned to Medora with Frank Foster's force of butchers.

moments.label: Knocked out by Ware in Chicago
